entries.providerBehavior: GitLab can report more than one pipeline for one commit (a branch pipeline and a merge-request pipeline) instead of a single pipeline.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: read-pipeline-run for the commit returns every reported pipeline, each with a distinct identity, closed-set job states, and trace evidence where the provider records a trace; no newest-wins singleton is selected.

entries.providerBehavior: GitLab merge status resolves asynchronously: values such as checking and unchecked mean the provider has not finished evaluating mergeability.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: Asynchronous native values normalize to non-terminal delivery review states only; they never report merged or closed while the native value is still evaluating.

entries.providerBehavior: GitLab may report merge_status and detailed_merge_status simultaneously with different meanings.
entries.expectedNormalizedOutcome: detailed_merge_status is authoritative when present and merge_status is the fallback; an unknown native value fails visibly instead of silently flattening to a delivery state.
